title: Anchored Rubric and Synthetic Control Evals for Config Rollouts
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Purpose: Design and ship an evaluation methodology that pairs anchored rubric items with synthetic control prompt cohorts to detect and quantify quality regressions caused by model/config changes. Background: Current eval pipelines surface composite score deltas but are sensitive to prompt-mix and judge variance; recent rollout incidents showed silent quality shifts in niche cohorts. Goals: (1) Define a small set of anchor prompts (human-labeled gold standards) per workload to act as stable calibration points across rollouts; (2) Create synthetic control cohorts (input transformations and perturbations) to amplify regressions that manifest only under specific tokenization/kv-cache/use-case patterns; (3) Produce an aggregation and debiasing procedure for judge ensembles (LLM-as-judge + human labels) that yields calibrated, interpretable delta estimates and uncertainty bands; (4) Integrate automated alerts into the Console with cohort-level drift signal and recommended rollback thresholds. Success criteria: - Anchors cover >90% of observed failure modes in retrospective incident analysis - Calibrated judge ensemble reduces false positive regression alerts by >=40% vs current pipeline - Alerting precision for high-severity regressions (customer-impact = high) >= 85% in staged rollouts - Full integration into pre-rollout gates for canary and A/B flows.
scope: In-scope: anchor prompt selection process; synthetic control generator scripts; LLM-as-judge weighting and temperature calibration; aggregation logic and uncertainty quantification; Console alert integration and dashboards. Out-of-scope: major UI redesigns, changes to model training data, non-eval telemetry collection.
deliverables: 1) Anchor prompt registry (Confluence + JSON manifest) 2) Synthetic control generator and test harness (GH) 3) Calibrated judge ensemble library with temperature/weight tuning scripts 4) Eval aggregation pipeline update + explainability fields 5) Console cohort dashboard and automated regression alert rule set 6) Post-rollout validation playbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Anchor selection becomes stale as models evolve. Mitigation: quarterly anchor review process and automated anchor health checks. Risk: LLM-as-judge introduces systematic bias correlated with model family. Mitigation: enforce hybrid judge ensemble (LLM judge + human spot checks) and per-cohort reweighting. Risk: Too many alerts from synthetic amplifications. Mitigation: calibrate signal thresholds to precision targets using retrospective holdout.
timeline: Week 1-2: anchor selection + labeling (PM, Research, Contractors). Week 3: synthetic cohort generator and unit tests. Week 4: judge ensemble experiments and calibration; temperature scaling + weight sweep. Week 5: pipeline integration + dashboard. Week 6: canary rollout and validation; iterate on thresholds.
stakeholders: PM: Sofia Patel; Eng: Liam Chen (lead), Maya Rivera; Research: Dr. Aisha Raman; Design: Carlos Mendes; SRE/Console: Priya Kapoor; Customer Success: Elena Novak
artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Anchored+Rubric+and+Synthetic+Controls; GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/1423; Playbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/eval-rollout-playbook-v0.1; Dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EvalDashboardMock
testing_plan: 1) Retrospective replay: run new method on past 12 months of rollouts and compare detected regressions vs known incidents. 2) Shadow runs: run new aggregation in parallel for 2 weeks on canaries. 3) Human spot-checks: sample N=200 anchor items for each major cohort during calibration. 4) Canary triggers: block rollout if calibrated delta > threshold with 95% CI excluding zero.
comments: 2025-02-19 Sofia Patel: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed on anchor definition: small, human-labeled prompts that probe critical behaviors (safety, factuality, instruction-following). Action: Research to propose initial 40 anchors by 2025-02-25.
2025-02-25 Maya Rivera: Research delivered 46 candidate anchors; we shortlisted 28 after redundancy dedupe. Raised question about cross-lingual anchors — decided to scope EN + ES for MVP.

2025-03-01 Liam Chen: Prototyped synthetic control generator (tokenization-edge cases + prefix caching patterns). Unit tests added. Observed that some configs change tokenization causing false drift signals; added normalization step before scoring.

2025-03-04 Dr. Aisha Raman: Ran judge ensemble sweep across 3 model families. Found LLM-judge overconfident on brevity prompts. Temperature scaling + human-judge bias correction reduced overconfidence; recommend ensemble weights [LLM:0.6, human:0.4] as starting point for this workload.
